claims.text: The selected alloy is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The initial alloy is a random, single-phase disordered solid solution with minimal chemical short-range order.
Controlled thermal annealing can induce measurable SRO in HfNbTaTiZr without causing secondary-phase precipitation.
The degree of chemical SRO controls whether superconductivity emerges and the magnitude of its transition temperature.
SRO produces local chemically ordered clusters.
Chemical SRO modifies local lattice vibrations and the phonon density of states in HfNbTaTiZr.
Increasing SRO shifts and sharpens high-frequency phonon modes.
The SRO-induced phonon-spectrum changes enhance the electron–phonon coupling constant.
Enhanced electron–phonon coupling opens a superconducting gap and raises the transition temperature relative to the random state.
SRO-enhanced samples will exhibit a superconducting transition distinct from, and likely higher in temperature than, that of the random baseline.
The superconducting transition will be observable through a resistivity drop and a Meissner response.
Phonon spectroscopy will reveal mode shifts correlated with the degree of SRO.
The random baseline alloy will have weak or absent superconducting signatures.
The proposed mechanism applies only within a composition and processing window where SRO can form without phase separation or secondary phases.
The proposed superconducting effect is expected in the low-temperature regime, typically below 5 K.
Competing scattering and disorder effects may counterbalance the proposed SRO-induced enhancement.
If SRO-enhanced and random controls have indistinguishable superconducting properties, electron–phonon signatures, and phonon spectra, the proposed causal mechanism is falsified.
